title: 2027 Audi Q7: Prices, Reviews & Pictures - CarGurus.com
summary: Explore the 2027 Audi Q7 with CarGurus reviews, pricing insights, comparisons, news and expert analysis.
body_markdown:
## Look & feel


8/10


Given how long it’s been since the previous-generation Q7 debuted, it shouldn’t be surprising that this third-generation model makes a clean break when it comes to styling. The new Q7 has a cleaner look that emphasizes proportions over detailing to make it look like the luxury SUV most customers will expect, with less of a uniquely Audi visual statement than the previous two generations. It’s a big, boxy SUV with lots of presence, but there are plenty of those in this segment.


Audi is now focusing more on lighting technology than styling elements, in part because it can now legally use the matrix technology that’s been available in Europe for over a decade in the U.S. The lighting elements are aimed individually, so at night you can drive with your high beams on more or less all the time, allowing the software to point the light away from oncoming cars. During a brief demo, we also found the matrix provides more illumination to side than conventional LED headlights. That makes it easier for drivers to spot deer running out into the road, and for passengers to see what’s outside the car.


Both the headlights and taillights have dual stacked elements, with programmable sections on top. But the OLED taillights have safety-related functions like small warning triangles (probably too small for following drivers to easily see) that pop up when the hazards are on, the ability to pulse at full brightness when someone approaches from behind too quickly. Turn signal warning lights are also projected onto the road surface at night—even at highway speeds.


The 2027 Q7 is available in Premium, Premium Plus, and Prestige trim levels. The base Premium model comes standard with 20-inch wheels on all-season run-flat tires. The Premium Plus and Prestige can both be equipped with 21s as either a standalone option or as part of the Black Optic Package that also includes blacked-out trim. A Launch Edition option for the Prestige adds 22-inch wheels, sportier S Line styling elements, and an illuminated grille similar to the one on the SQ7 performance model.


The interior exudes style and quality in a way we haven’t seen in other recent Audi models. Most shiny black plastic has been banished, replaced by nicer looking matte-finish surfaces. The wood trim is tasteful, like what you’d expect to find in the lobby of a trendy hotel. And there are some neat design elements, like the curved door panels that reach out like fingers to the dashboard. Leather upholstery is standard (with Nappa leather on the top Prestige model) along with a panoramic glass sunroof. It’s a true sunroof that can open, with optional dimming. Power rear sunshades and power doors are also available, upping the luxury factor significantly.


## Performance


9/10


The 2027 Q7 comes standard with a turbocharged 2.9-liter V6 connected to an eight-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive (AWD). This single powertrain offering replaces the previous 2.0-liter turbo-four and 3.0-liter V6, but makes 94 horsepower and 73 pound-feet of torque more than even the latter, formerly optional engine, at 429 hp and 442 lb-ft.


That in turn decreases the manufacturer-estimated zero to 60 mph time by 0.7 second, to 4.8 seconds (the top speed is still electronically limited to 130 mph). That’s not bad for a 5,137-pound SUV. And because Audi offers more standard horsepower, the Q7 is also quicker than the (also redesigned for 2027) BMW X5 despite the Bimmer’s not being burdened with a third row. In the Mercedes-Benz GLE lineup, you’ll have to step up to the V8-powered GLE 580 4Matic to get quicker acceleration.


Behind the wheel, this translates into higher-than-expected levels of fun for a family vehicle. The V6 is never caught flat-footed, the transmissions shifts are imperceptible, and while it’s clearly been artificially enhanced, the engine sound in Dynamic mode (there are Balanced, Comfort, Offroad, and Individual modes as well), provides the sporty ambience parents who were forced to trade their S5s and RS3s for this will appreciate. And Audi’s signature AWD was as good as ever in wet conditions.


Steel-spring suspension is standard, but an air suspension system with automatic load levelling is also available. For 2027, the air suspension adds an exit-assist function that allows the Q7 to kneel 2.4 inches, like a city bus. An SQ7 performance model with a more powerful engine and sportier chassis features also returns for 2027, but we’ll cover that in a separate review.


The Q7 surpassed expectations in the ride and handling department. Defying Audi stereotypes, it didn’t experience much understeer even in low-grip conditions. Equipped with the optional air suspension, our test car exhibited reasonably good body control for a big SUV, while providing the pillowed ride one should expected with air springs. The steering wasn’t the most communicative, but it was more consistent in effort than in other recent Audi models we’ve driven. Our test car also had the optional rear-axle steering, which can’t totally erase this SUV’s bulk, but does provide sharper turn-in and contributed to an impressive sense of stability at highway speeds.


## Form & function


8/10


As is typical for three-row SUVs, the Q7 is available as a seven-seater, or with second-row captain’s chairs that reduce the total number of seats to six, but create a more luxurious environment in the middle row. The latter is a new feature for 2027, and those seats are power adjustable and come with their own climate controls. Second-row headroom and legroom is also comparable to most rivals, although the Mercedes-Benz GLE has a bit more legroom in this row.


The new Q7 has the same wheelbase as the outgoing model, but is 1.7 inches wider and 2.8 inches taller. Audi claims the flatter roof and more upright D-pillar improve third-row headroom. Indeed, the Q7 offers appreciably more than the Acura MDX, Lexus TX, and Volvo XC90. Third-row legroom matches the Acura, but trails the Lexus and Volvo. Standard power-tilting second-row seats that work even with a child seat installed improve access over the previous-generation Q7.


Both the second and third rows also power fold at the touch of a button to make loading cargo more convenient. As with most three-row vehicles, the 15.1 cubic feet of cargo space behind the third row isn’t a lot considering the overall size of the vehicle. And while it’s 1.5 cubic feet more than the 2026 Q7 had, it’s still less than some other three-row midsize SUVs. That’s also the case with the 37.7 cubic feet behind the second row with captain’s chairs, although the standard fold-flat bench offers 43.9 cubic feet of space. The 78.1 cubic feet behind the first row is more competitive, as is the Q7’s 7,700-pound maximum towing capacity.


Up front is where the Q7 earns its luxury billing. There’s class-competitive headroom and legroom, available heated, ventilated, and massaging seats, as well as heated armrests. Even without those features, the seats are both comfortable and offer an appropriate level of bolstering for what Audi intended to be a sportier-than-average SUV.


## Technology


8/10


The Audi Digital Stage screen array is new to the Q7 for 2027, but can already be found in nearly every other Audi model. An 11.9-inch digital instrument cluster and 14.5-inch touchscreen encircle the driver, while the front passenger gets their own 12.3-inch touchscreen with filters to avoid distracting the driver. A head-up display is also available and front-seat occupants get high-speed magnetic wireless device chargers. USB-C ports provide power in the second and third rows, including a pair embedded in the backs of the front seats for middle-row occupants.


The current version of Audi’s MMI infotainment system is Android-based, but retains wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, as well as a distinctly Audi look. Richly-detailed Google Earth satellite maps—one of the standout features of previous Audi infotainment systems that the automaker dropped—are also back, and available across all three screens.


Satellite maps weren’t the only graphics that impressed. When you switch drive modes, a giant, well-rendered image of the Q7 takes over the screen. There are equally well-rendered images of the seats and dashboard for the massage and climate-control menus, respectively. Temperature, fan speed, and even the air vents can only be controlled via the screen, which is less than ideal. And only the most attentive copilots will find use of the dedicated passenger screen.


An available voice recognition system can handle some in-vehicle functions like turning on the seat massagers, and can also answer general knowledge questions thanks to ChatGPT integration. However, it and the Google satellite imagery are only available as part of the Connect Nav digital services package, which comes as a three-year trial but requires a paid subscription after that.


Also new for 2027 is a 22-speaker, 1,360-watt, Bang & Olufsen 4D audio system. Available as a standalone option on the Premium Plus and Prestige trims, it has headrest speakers that let the driver take phone calls without disturbing passengers, and in-seat actuators that vibrate in sync with music. Neither of these features are new to luxury vehicles in general, but returning Audi customers will find them novel.


## Safety


7/10


The 2027 Q7 comes standard with expected driver-assistance features like forward collision warning, automatic emergency braking, blind spot monitoring, rear cross traffic alert, a 360-degree camera system, and lane departure warning. For 2027, the latter includes Normal and Reduced modes for different road conditions. A dash cam and hands-free highway driving system are optional. We only had a limited opportunity to test out the latter, but during that brief period it didn’t misbehave.


The redesign also brings some new features that cover more than the basics. A “trained parking” automated parking feature allows the Q7 to semi-autonomously park itself (with supervision), while available trailer-sway assist and trailer-maneuvering assist features let drivers take advantage of the Q7’s 7,700-pound maximum towing capacity.


Safety ratings from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) and National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) were not available at the time of writing.


## Cost-effectiveness


7/10


The 2027 Audi Q7 is EPA-rated at 19 mpg combined (16 mpg city, 23 mpg highway). It’s worth noting that many of the Q7’s rivals offer hybrid and plug-in hybrid powertrains. The Q7’s twin-turbo V6 offers great performance, but it can’t match the efficiency of those powertrains.


Pricing starts at $72,295 for the Premium trim level, including a $1,395 destination charge. The Premium Plus starts at $76,695 with destination, and the Prestige starts at $86,295 after destination. Our Prestige car was also a Launch Edition equipped with the Bang & Olufsen 4D audio system, a trailer hitch, and captain’s chairs, bringing its as-tested price to approximately $94,000.


Audi claims the 2027 model starts $1,400 higher than a comparably-equipped 2027 model, but that’s with some additional standard equipment. Pricing also remains competitive with Audi’s German rivals. The Q7 is within a few hundred dollars of a base AWD BMW X5 and is a few grand less than a Mercedes-Benz GLE 450 4Matic with a six-cylinder engine an AWD. The Audi will also likely be easier to live with than the tech-heavy BMW and Mercedes.


If you just need three rows of seats, the Acura MDX, Lexus TX, and Volvo XC90 all undercut the Q7. But the price difference shrinks when cars are comparably equipped. The Audi also offers a sportier driving experience than the Volvo and a more upscale feel than the Acura or Lexus. Overall, it’s a very competitive model for its segment.
